    Endomorphism-invariant submodules and the (brick-discrete) characterization #

    Shows that every weight on submodules of a brick M attains its maximum on an End_R(M)-invariant submodule (exists_endInvariant_weight_maximizer), and combines normalized submodule polytopes with finite-field witness bounds to prove isEFinite_iff_endo_brick ((E-fin) ⇔ (brick-discrete) over an arbitrary field).

      Hom into an invariant submodule has ground dimension divisible by the dimension of the brick endomorphism ring. Its quotient is bounded in terms of the source and the endolength alone.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.finite_semistability_loci_at_bounded_endolength {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] (r : ℕ) :
      {s : Set (ProjectiveClass R) | ∃ (X : FGModuleCat R), IsBrick X ∧ endolength k X ≤ r ∧ s = {g : ProjectiveClass R | ((projectiveClassWeight k) g).IsSemistable X}}.Finite

      At bounded endolength, a finite set of data describes the integral semistability loci. The data consist of the normalized Hom coordinates of the whole module and the set of those of its invariant submodules.
